records.plant_name: Monarch Rock Air data center campus (Rockford)
records.monitor_reason: The campus has power generation mentioned in state records, but no generating unit, fuel or size is named.

verifications.note: Names Monarch Rock Air, Friday Road, a 1,400 megawatt phased data center and associated power generation.

records.researcher_notes: A Rock River Current article from June 2026, based on state incentive records, says Monarch Rock Air plans a multibuilding data center campus with associated power generation on Friday Road in Rockford. It is described as a 1,400 MW phased data center, which is the size of the campus and not of any generator. No source I found names gas engines or turbines. The 250 MW of gas engines mentioned in the earlier task list could not be confirmed, and a Caterpillar order for a site called Monarch belongs to a West Virginia campus. Other reports describe grid power from ComEd. I looked for an Illinois EPA air permit notice and found none. Not found: fuel, number of engines and generating capacity. Check again for an air permit application.

records.monitor_reason: The source gives a 50 MW data center size and names no generating unit.
records.researcher_notes: A Data Center Dynamics article from August 2025 says Hut 8's Illinois Project 4 totals 50 MW. It does not say where the site is and does not name any generators. A separate local report about a Hut 8 proposal in Logan County says the company has not decided between gas or diesel backup generators, but it is not confirmed that this is Project 4. No Illinois EPA permit notice names Hut 8. Not found: town, power source and any engines or turbines.

records.plant_name: Joliet Technology Center data center campus
records.monitor_reason: The campus is approved at 1.8 GW of data center load, but no generating unit is named.
records.researcher_notes: The Joliet city council approved the PowerHouse Data Centers and Hillwood campus in March 2026. A Data Center Dynamics article says it will offer up to 1.8 GW at full build in four phases, each with its own substation. A data center listing says the developer is securing its own electricity supply, but names no fuel or equipment. No Illinois EPA permit notice names the campus. Not found: any on-site gas turbines or engines and their size.
